excerpt: You hold part of the Congo Basin forest, rivers that already light two thirds of your grid, and a young nation of nearly thirty million.
paras: You hold part of the Congo Basin forest, rivers that already light two thirds of your grid, and a young nation of nearly thirty million. Your debt is sustainable but costly. Let the forest and the rivers carry cheaper capital than the market now offers you.

Your partners are building with you. In June 2026 the World Bank approved $425 million for the first phase of the Douala–Bangui economic corridor. In 2025 it approved $200 million for water security and $200 million for your cities and land. In January 2026 you returned to the international market and raised $750 million.

The work ahead is plain, and it is worth saying plainly. Each of you uses about 251 kilowatt hours of electricity a year, a quarter of what a decent life needs, and fewer than one in three cooks with clean fuel. At the last count, in 2019, seventy-two in every hundred of your children reached the end of primary school unable to read a simple text. Sixty-one in every hundred of you cannot always count on enough good food. Power sets your Coverage today, at 25.1 out of 100, with reading and food close behind. Each of them is within your reach.

Now imagine that same resolve turned toward every home in the country. Picture Perfect Cameroon: a morning when every family cooks with clean fuel and sits down to a full table; when every tap runs clean and every home has a safe toilet; when every child walks to a school where a teacher is waiting, and reads with ease by the age of ten; when every mother lives within reach of a clinic with the lights on, and every young person finds work that pays. And no Cameroonian falls below a decent life, because the nation has decided that none will.
quote: Your forest stores the world’s carbon. Let the world pay for it in cheaper capital.
